records.summary: 667 Commercial St is in the CCB (Chinatown Community Business District) zoning district where restaurants are a conditional use on the first story. The records show this address has operated as a restaurant since at least 1998, with Planning approvals in 1998 and 2014 confirming continuation of the restaurant use. The immediate area is extremely dense with food and beverage establishments: 32 registered food/drink businesses and 14 active ABC on-sale licenses within 500 feet. The base rate within 1,000 feet shows only 7 dated Planning decisions in the last 5 years (1 approved, 3 approved with conditions, 3 withdrawn, 0 denied)—too few to calculate an approval rate—but all restaurant applications in the CCB district on this block have been approved as continuation of existing uses or as permitted/conditional uses under Planning Code Section 810.

comparables.why_comparable: ABC Type 41 beer & wine license for existing restaurant in the CCB district at 653 Clay St, 44 meters away on the same block. Agency referral for continuation of existing restaurant use, approved in 28 days.
comparables.key_takeaway: Planning approved Type 41 for an existing restaurant in CCB as a continuation of use without conditions or a hearing. This agency referral shows the department treats beer-and-wine service as permitted in conjunction with an established restaurant in the CCB district.

comparables.why_comparable: DPH restaurant referral for the same 653 Clay St address (44m away) in CCB, approved 23 days after filing. Confirms continuation of existing restaurant use under Planning Code Section 810.
comparables.key_takeaway: Planning's approval language ('conditionally permitted in the C-C-B Zoning District per PC Section 810. Continuation of existing use') confirms that established restaurants in CCB may continue operating without triggering a new conditional use process for routine permits.

comparables.why_comparable: Limited restaurant approval at 660 Sacramento St in CCB, only 13 meters away, approved in 17 days. Planning cited prior Building Permit 9021345 establishing the use.
comparables.key_takeaway: This agency referral demonstrates that Planning approves continuation of previously established restaurant uses in CCB by administrative review, relying on prior building permits to confirm the legal status, with no hearing or conditions.

comparables.why_comparable: Limited restaurant (d.b.a. Neutral) at 683 Commercial St in CCB, 12 meters away on the same block, approved in 29 days. Same zoning district and immediate vicinity.
comparables.key_takeaway: Planning approved this limited restaurant as principally permitted in CCB per Section 810.43 through an agency referral with no conditions, showing that restaurant continuations on this block proceed administratively.

comparables.why_comparable: ABC Type 47 and 58 full-bar licenses for existing restaurant at 653 Commercial St in CCB, 21 meters away, approved in 27 days. Same block, same district, higher-level alcohol license.
comparables.key_takeaway: Planning approved even a Type 47 full-bar license in CCB at this address as a continuation of existing conditional use, citing Section 810.44 and 178. If full liquor was approved as a continuation, beer-and-wine (Type 41) at an established restaurant will follow the same path.

comparables.why_comparable: ABC Type 41 for restaurant at 550 Kearny St in C-3-O district, 68 meters away, approved in 19 days. Continuation of existing restaurant use with beer and wine service.
comparables.key_takeaway: This C-3-O approval (an adjacent downtown district) for Type 41 as continuation of existing use took under three weeks and had no conditions, showing the administrative path for adding beer and wine to an established restaurant in this area.

comparables.why_comparable: ABC Type 41 for restaurant (K Five Fifty) at 550 Kearny St in C-3-O, 68m away, approved in 5 days. Fast approval for beer and wine at a restaurant near Chinatown.
comparables.key_takeaway: Planning approved this Type 41 in five working days as principally permitted in C-3-O. The record shows no concerns about the high density of licenses in the area, and the quick turnaround signals that continuation-of-use alcohol referrals are routine.

comparables.why_comparable: Limited restaurant continuation at 600 Kearny St in CCB, 40 meters away, approved in 9 days. Same zoning district, same block, DPH health referral approved quickly.
comparables.key_takeaway: This nine-day approval for a limited-restaurant continuation in CCB shows Planning treats routine health and ABC referrals for existing restaurants as ministerial; no conditions were imposed.

comparables.why_comparable: Health-Restaurant application at 801 Kearny St in CCB, 195m away, denied after three years. Only denial in the candidate set; took from June 2016 to August 2019.
comparables.key_takeaway: This is the only denial among CCB restaurant applications in the area. The record gives no stated reason for the denial, and the three-year timeline suggests the applicant may have failed to complete requirements or the use was never legally established, not that Planning denied continuation of a lawful restaurant.

comparables.why_comparable: Conditional Use Authorization to convert basement retail into a new 5,000 sq ft restaurant at 838 Grant Ave in CVR district, 198m away, approved with conditions after six months including midnight closing.
comparables.key_takeaway: This is a use_decision for a new restaurant requiring a Planning Commission hearing. It shows the difference: a new or changed restaurant use needs CUA with hours limits and conditions, whereas continuation of an existing restaurant (as here) proceeds administratively with no hearing.

patterns.pattern: Continuation of existing restaurant use in CCB: every agency referral for an established restaurant in the CCB district on or near Commercial St was approved administratively in 5–29 days with zero conditions, citing Planning Code Section 810 continuation provisions.

ABC Type 41 beer-and-wine licenses approved without conditions: Planning approved every Type 41 referral for existing restaurants in CCB and adjacent C-3-O within 28 days, treating the license as permitted in conjunction with the established restaurant use.

Even Type 47 full-bar licenses approved as continuation: one record at 653 Commercial St (21m away, same CCB block) shows Planning approved a Type 47 full-liquor license for an existing restaurant as a continuation of conditional use in 27 days with no new conditions.

High ABC license density not a barrier for continuations: all approved referrals within 70 meters proceeded despite 14 active ABC on-sale licenses within 500 feet; Planning made no reference to undue concentration in any approval.

New restaurant uses require CUA hearings with conditions: the one Conditional Use Authorization in the set (838 Grant Ave CVR) required a Planning Commission hearing, took six months, and imposed midnight closing, soundproofing, odor control, and sidewalk maintenance conditions.

Only one denial in three years, no stated reason: one health-restaurant application at 801 Kearny CCB was denied after three years with no explanation in the record; every other restaurant application in CCB was approved.

approvals.summary: Adding alcohol to an existing restaurant in CCB is an intensification of a conditional use that triggers further review under Planning Code Section 178, though the records do not establish whether the business is formula retail or what occupancy the space holds.

findings.text: Planning approved restaurant use at this address in 1998 and 2014 as continuation of existing use permitted under Planning Code Section 810.42 and 810.43 in the CCB district.

A new restaurant in CCB is a conditional use per Planning Code Section 810, but Planning Code Section 178 requires a new conditional use authorization when an existing conditional use is significantly altered, enlarged or intensified.

Adding beer and wine service to an established restaurant has been treated by Planning as continuation of use: at 653 Clay St (44m away, CCB), Planning approved a Type 41 license in 28 days as permitted in conjunction with existing restaurant use, and at 653 Commercial St (21m away, CCB), Planning approved a Type 47 full-bar license in 27 days as continuation of existing conditional use.

The description does not state whether the business is part of a chain sharing its name, look or menu with other locations. Formula retail is not permitted for restaurants in CCB per Planning Code Section 810.
A pending Miscellaneous Permit (2022-011138MIS) was filed at this address on November 14, 2022 with no description in the public record; its purpose is unknown.

findings.text: No ABC license of any type is on file at 667 Commercial St as of December 5, 2022.

Census tract 611.01 holds 55 active on-sale retail licenses against 6 authorized per ABC's September 2026 census tract authorizations, placing it in undue concentration under California Business and Professions Code Section 23958.4.

ABC Type 41 is a non-quota license issued directly by ABC for bona fide eating places, but undue-concentration tracts require a Public Convenience or Necessity finding from the city and can add one to three months to ABC's 55–65 day timeline.

Planning approved Type 41 licenses for existing restaurants in the immediate area (653 Clay St in 2020, 550 Kearny St in 2021 and 2019) as continuation of use with no reference to undue concentration in the approval language.

expected_conditions.condition: ABC Type 41 license limits service to beer and wine only, no distilled spirits, and minors are allowed on the premises with food service.
expected_conditions.basis: Type 41 is defined as on-sale beer and wine for eating places under California Business and Professions Code Section 23394. Every Type 41 approval in the comparables (653 Clay St, 550 Kearny St, 653 Commercial St) carried these limits by license type.

expected_conditions.condition: Bona fide eating place requirement: the premises must be regularly and principally used for the service of meals to guests, with a kitchen, seating, and food sales exceeding alcohol sales.
expected_conditions.basis: Type 41 licenses are restricted to bona fide eating places per California Business and Professions Code Section 23038. ABC enforces this through inspections and sales ratio audits. The permit catalog states minors are allowed, which distinguishes it from bar licenses.

expected_conditions.condition: Thirty-day public posting at the premises during the ABC application period, with ABC's notice placard visible from the street.
expected_conditions.basis: ABC requires a 30-day posting at the premises for all original applications and premises-to-premises transfers per California Business and Professions Code Section 24013. The permit catalog notes this posting period and that local protests can trigger a Public Convenience or Necessity hearing.

expected_conditions.condition: Responsible Beverage Service (RBS) certification for all alcohol servers and managers within 60 days of hire, registered with ABC at $3 plus course fees of $10–$25 per person.
expected_conditions.basis: California AB 1221 mandates RBS training for every person who serves alcohol and their managers. The permit catalog entry for ca.rbs_training states this is required within 60 days and that ABC inspects for certification lists on site.

expected_conditions.condition: If Planning treats the addition of alcohol as continuation of use, expect no new operating-hour restrictions beyond existing restaurant hours; if it requires a new CUA, expect a midnight closing condition.
expected_conditions.basis: The one CUA for a new restaurant in the comparables (838 Grant Ave CVR, case 2021-008505CUA) imposed a midnight closing condition. By contrast, every agency referral for continuation of an existing restaurant with alcohol (653 Clay, 653 Commercial, 550 Kearny) had no new hours conditions.

filing_playbook.action: Contact San Francisco Planning by phone at (628) 652-7600 or email to confirm in writing that adding beer and wine service qualifies as continuation of use under Planning Code Sections 810.44 and 178, and does not require a new Conditional Use Authorization.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: State that you operate an existing restaurant at 667 Commercial St that has been legally established since at least 1998 (Planning approval MA9900405) and 2014 (MB1400941), and you wish to add ABC Type 41 beer and wine service. Ask whether this is treated as continuation of the existing conditional use or as an intensification requiring a new CUA hearing. Reference comparable approvals at 653 Commercial St (Type 47 approved as continuation, case 2017-013358MIS) and 653 Clay St (Type 41 approved as continuation, case 2020-010940MIS). Request a written determination or a pre-application meeting to confirm the pathway before filing ABC or health applications.

filing_playbook.action: If Planning confirms continuation of use, file the ABC Type 41 original application online through ABC's online portal, including the signed lease, entity documents, seller's permit, and the Planning Department's written confirmation that the restaurant use is established.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: In the ABC application, describe the premises as a bona fide eating place with a full commercial kitchen, table seating, and meals served during all hours of alcohol service. Attach Planning's written confirmation that the restaurant use is legally established and authorized to continue in the CCB district per Planning Code Section 810. Submit the signed lease, California Secretary of State entity registration, seller's permit, and photos of the interior showing kitchen and dining areas. ABC will route the application to SFPD and Planning for 30-day referral review, then post a notice at the premises for 30 days. Budget 60–120 days if unprotested; add one to three months if the census tract's undue concentration triggers a Public Convenience or Necessity finding request from the city.

filing_playbook.action: File for or renew the San Francisco Business Registration Certificate and the Health Permit to Operate through the SF Department of Public Health online portal, confirming continuation of the existing restaurant use.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: State that the restaurant use at 667 Commercial St continues as previously approved by Planning in 1998 and 2014, and that beer and wine service is being added under an ABC Type 41 application. DPH will route the health permit application to Planning for a zoning referral; Planning should approve it administratively as continuation of use if step 1 confirmed that pathway. Attach the ABC application receipt, the certified food safety manager certificate, and proof of workers' compensation insurance. The health permit referral typically takes 14–45 days for administrative approval.

filing_playbook.action: Obtain a California Seller's Permit from CDTFA (free, online, often same-day) and register for California EDD payroll taxes if not already done, as both are prerequisites for the ABC license.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Register online through the CDTFA portal for the seller's permit (no fee) and the EDD e-Services for Business portal for employer registration (no fee). ABC will not issue the Type 41 license until the seller's permit number is on file. If you already hold these registrations, provide the account numbers on the ABC application.

filing_playbook.action: Enroll all alcohol-serving staff and managers in ABC-approved Responsible Beverage Service (RBS) training within 60 days of hire, and post the certification list on site for ABC inspections.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Register each employee on the ABC RBS Portal ($3 per person), complete an approved RBS course (about $10–$25 per person), and pass the exam. Download the certificates and keep a current list of certified staff on the premises. ABC inspectors will ask for this list during routine inspections and at the time of license issuance.

timeline_cost.notes: Timeline of 60–210 days and cost of $1,470–$2,600 are for approvals when granted, covering the Conditional Use Authorization (if required) and the Health Permit to Operate. ABC Type 41 application: 60–120 days per the permit catalog if unprotested; one to three months longer if census tract 611.01's undue concentration requires a Public Convenience or Necessity finding from the city. Health permit to operate: 14–45 days per the catalog entry. The timeline assumes Planning confirms continuation of use; if Planning requires a new Conditional Use Authorization, add 120–300 days and $3,100–$15,000 per catalog entry sf.conditional_use_authorization, based on the one CUA comparable at 838 Grant Ave that took 183 days from filing to approval. Government fees: ABC Type 41 application $1,000–$1,600, health permit to operate $470–$1,000 (2026–27 schedule). Not included: San Francisco Business Registration Certificate $55–$700 (prerequisite, typically $55–$95 for a small restaurant), California Seller's Permit (free), EDD employer registration (free), RBS training $13–$55 per employee, ASCAP and BMI music licenses $600–$5,000 combined (not government fees), and any building permit if a change of occupancy is determined. The pending Miscellaneous Permit 2022-011138MIS filed November 14, 2022 at this address may affect the timeline; verify its status with Planning before filing.
